title: Coordinated gating scenarios & safety handoff (sandbox) - WIP
content:
Purpose / scope:
- Working sketch: define a relatively lightweight, reproducible ceremony for progressive exposure + safe handoffs across product, infra, SRE, and CS for inference-facing changes (model, runtime, config).
- Target: launches where user-visible behavior could change (reranking, response shape, hallucination risk, cost/latency tradeoffs). Not for purely UI-only toggles.
- Goal: reduce surprise for downstream teams, shorten time-to-decision, and provide clear metrics + human checkpoints for roll/stop/escalate.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- 4-stage exposure: 0. internal canary (ci/smoke), 1. closed cohort (engineers + small biz segment), 2. staggered public slices (traffic slices, 0.1% -> 5%), 3. Ramp-to-mean or rollback.
- Each stage has prerequisite checks, observation windows, owner sign-off, and automatic abort criteria.
- Handoff ritual: 15-min sync + short roll document + Slack signal channel + incident trigger matrix.

Ceremony roles (minimal):
- Release Lead (RL): coordinates stages, owns the roll doc + go/no-go. (product or PM rotate)
- Service Owner (SO): infra/serving-runtime engineer for the model/route. Responsible for quick mitigation steps (traffic-cut, variant-swap).
- Oncall/Triage (SRE): monitors platform SLOs, runs rollback if infra thresholds exceeded.
- Quality Owner (QO): ML engineer or product QA responsible for model-behavior metrics (hallucination, truthfulness, safety signals).
- CS / Solutions Rep: flag customer-affecting issues and validate user impact.

Pre-launch checklist (must be green before stage 1):
- Baseline metrics recorded (last 7d): latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, token-cost per request, model quality baseline (sample eval set).
- Roll doc created: short one-pager (purpose, change summary, risk profile, rollback steps).
- Automatic feature flags ready (span-coded slices), throttles, safety filters enabled.
- Observability: dashboards prebuilt (cost/latency/per-route), synthetic probe configured, synthetic golden prompts for QA.
- Communication channel: #rollouts-ops private channel + stakeholder watchlist.

Stage definitions and gates:
- Stage 0: CI & internal smoke
  - Traffic: internal only (CI, dev accounts).
  - Observation window: 15–30m.
  - Checks: basic smoke, KV cache behavior, no obvious regressions in p95 latency.
  - Signoff: SO 

- Stage 1: Closed cohort (early reviewers)
  - Traffic: <0.1% or explicit user list (eng + beta customers).
  - Window: 2–4 hours (rolling).
  - Checks: no >2x change in hallucination proxy on golden prompts, error rate <= baseline + 0.1pp, p95 <= baseline + 30%.
  - Human: QO reviews sample outputs, decides go/no-go.

- Stage 2: Staggered public slices
  - Traffic pattern: ramp schedule (0.1% -> 1% -> 5%) at configurable intervals (default: every 2–4 hours).
  - Observation window per step: 2–6 hours depending on sensitivity.
  - Checks (automated):
    - Latency SLOs: p95 and p99 within configured guardrails.
    - Cost delta: token-cost per request not above X% (configurable by RL).
    - Safety signals: profanity filter hits, hallucination proxy delta, high-uncertainty outputs > threshold.
    - Business signal: downstream conversion/CTR delta within tolerance.
  - Manual: RL + QO + SO quick sync after each step; explicit signoff to move to next slice.

- Stage 3: Ramp-to-mean or rollback
  - Continue ramp to target allocation or fallback to older model/route.
  - If stabilized for 24–72h with metrics within tolerances, mark final.
  - Post-mortem: if any abort triggered, perform incident review and classify root cause (model, infra, traffic assumptions).

Automated abort criteria (examples):
- Infrastructure triggers (SRE auto abort): p99 latency > threshold for 3 consecutive windows OR sustained error rate > 1% above baseline for 15m.
- Quality triggers (QO auto abort): hallucination proxy increase > 30% on golden prompt batch AND manual spot-check confirms.
- Business triggers: conversion drop > 5% over 1h for primary funnel.
- Cost triggers: unit token cost > budgeted multiplier (default 2x) for more than 30 minutes.

Handoff ritual (practical checklist):
- 15-min pre-stage meeting in #rollouts-ops: RL runs through the roll doc, owners confirm dashboards and abort commands.
- Post-stage check-in (10 min): rapid assessment, clear log of decision (next ramp / hold / rollback).
- Slack signals: use pinned emoji reactions in the channel for quick state (eyes = observed, check = go, stop sign = abort).
- Triage play: SO ready to cut traffic to previous variant with a single CLI/console command; SRE ready to escalate if system-level regressions.

Observability & instrumentation specifics (must-haves):
- Golden prompt suite: 40–100 targeted prompts covering safety, hallucination-prone contexts, token-length edge cases. Run every slice step automatically and surface deltas.
- Sampling: save 1% of raw interactions + deterministic sampling of failure cases for forensic analysis.
- Cost telemetry: per-route per-model token accounting and tag by rollout-id.
- Latency histograms: per-model and per-region p50/p95/p99 with 1m granularity.
- Canary logs: short-lived retention of raw canary traces (30d) and aggregated metrics (90d).

Simulation & pre-check (lightweight):
- Before public slices, run a quick simulator: replay last N minutes of traffic through new model variant at 0.5% sample using shadow mode (no external impact) and produce a cost/latency/quality delta report.
- If simulation shows >threshold negative regressions, pause and triage.

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve:
- How long should observation windows be for models with slow downstream business effects? (suggestion: tie to business half-life; e.g., weekly metrics require longer canary windows).
- Tolerances: centralize a small matrix of default tolerances by change-type (inference-only vs config vs model weight change) and allow RL overrides with documented rationale.
- Automation surface: what subset of gates can be automatically enforced vs human signoff required? (safety signals should default to auto-abort; small latency blips can be human-reviewed).
- Cross-region complexity: need region-aware rolling (e.g., EU first then NA for privacy-sensitive models).

Quick TODOs (next 2 weeks):
- Draft an automation prototype for golden-prompt auto-checks (ENG-5123). Owner: Diego.
- Create standard roll doc template in GDrive + quick generator in CLI. Owner: Samantha.
- Run live rehearsal for rollout ceremony with one low-risk change. Date: 2026-03-18. Owner: RL rotation (Marcus).
- Add rollout-id tags to cost telemetry pipeline (infra ticket INF-2998). Owner: SO.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the ceremony as light as possible. Avoid multi-hour meetings; prefer short pre-check and quick binary decisions.
- Emphasize synthetic probes and golden prompts — these save a ton of manual review time.
- Pressure-test runbooks quarterly with simulated aborts.

References / links (working):
- Confluence: rollout-contracts (link above)
- Existing playbooks: safety-net-and-reversion-playbook, staged-deployment-signal-runbook (these are related; this doc focuses on handoff cadence + simulation)
- Slack threads: #inc-experiment-runbook, #model-quality-watch

Appendix: example minimal roll doc (to be templated)
- Title: short
- Owner: RL, SO, QO
- Change summary: 2–3 lines
- Priority & risk: low/med/high (justification)
- Stages & ramp schedule (explicit percent + time)
- Key metrics & baselines (where to look)
- Abort commands (literal CLI / console action)
- Post-launch observation window & postmortem owner
- Rollout-id label

-- end --

(If you're reading: please add notes or objections inline. This is intentionally a lightweight proposal that we should iterate on.)
